answer: Stop sybils with a grove ocean zephyr: an agent bonds one ocean grove. Each cycle it raises one zephyr sail above the grove; verifiers match the sail's billow to the grove chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 groves at 17x: one sail billows once over one grove, its billow set by that zephyr through those trees, unrepeatable at a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents raise once, keep rights.
